_comment: Encatch helpdesk configuration (support tiers, SLAs, automation rules). Apply with apply.py; see README.md. Times are business hours on the desk's default business hours.
_default_team_comment: Every new ticket is assigned to this team (round robin among its online members). The team must have no business hours or SLA policy of its own.

support_tier_attribute.name: Support tier
support_tier_attribute.description: Customer's support tier; drives SLA policies. Empty = SaaS Standard.

_ticket_attributes_comment: Ticket (conversation) custom fields. My Tickets sets them from the signed token; SLA rules read ticket_tier first and fall back to the contact's Support tier. source_app empty = arrived by email.

ticket_attributes.name: Org ID
ticket_attributes.description: Encatch org the ticket was raised for, prefixed with its instance (e.g. prod-42)

ticket_attributes.name: Ticket support tier
ticket_attributes.description: Support tier of the ticket's org; overrides the contact's Support tier for SLAs

ticket_attributes.name: Requested priority
ticket_attributes.description: Priority the customer chose in My Tickets

ticket_attributes.name: Project ID
ticket_attributes.description: Encatch project the ticket is about, prefixed with its instance (e.g. prod-17)

ticket_attributes.name: Source app
ticket_attributes.description: Backend app that raised the ticket via My Tickets; empty = email

ticket_attributes.name: Encatch instance
ticket_attributes.description: Encatch instance the ticket came from via My Tickets: local, dev, uat or prod; empty = email

sla_policies.description: SaaS Standard tier: first reply within 48 business hours.

_sla_alerts_comment: Each policy warns 'warn_before' its deadline, then alerts on breach. Recipients: 'assigned_user', 'role:<Role>' (every agent with that role at apply time) or agent IDs (no emails live in this public repo). Breach alerts go to two named agents, IDs 34 and 35, not role:Admin: on 2026-10-22 the owner decided that agents made Admin later don't get them.
_new_ticket_alert_comment: Every new ticket also notifies these agents (in-app, and by email), from the same first-match rule that sets its SLA. Recipients: 'agent:<Full name>', 'team:<Team>' (each member) or 'role:<Role>', resolved to agents at apply time, so no emails live in this public repo. 'agent:Notification Desk' is the agent for the group mailbox; it isn't in any team, so it never gets tickets assigned. Its email must not be the Support inbox's own address, or each alert would come back as a new ticket. Subject and message are plain text; the email adds a link to the ticket.

new_ticket_alert.subject: New support ticket
new_ticket_alert.message: A new support ticket was raised. Open it with the link below.

_statuses_comment: Ticket statuses the rules and macros use, created when missing (matched by name; existing ones are left alone). Category waiting = waiting on someone else.
_auto_close_comment: Tickets left Waiting on customer: an automated reminder after reminder_after_hours, then an automated close after close_after_hours, both counted from the agent's last reply in clock hours (weekends included; automated replies don't restart the clock). Any customer reply reopens the ticket (status Open), which stops both. Time-trigger rules run hourly and only see tickets created in the last 30 days (libredesk). My Tickets shows Auto-closing as Waiting on you. Rules named 'Auto-close...' are owned by apply.py.

reminder_message: This is an automated reminder from Encatch Support.
We're waiting for your reply on this ticket. If we don't hear from you within 2 days, it will be closed automatically.
Still need help? Just reply to this email, or open the ticket from Support in your Encatch account, and it will stay open.
close_message: This is an automated message from Encatch Support.
This ticket was closed automatically because there's been no reply for 5 days.
If you still need help, reply to this email, or open the ticket from Support in your Encatch account, and it will reopen.

_tiers_comment: Priority -> SLA policy per tier. Tiers without a 'priorities' map get one SLA whatever the priority. A contact's tier comes only from its Support tier field.
_subject_tags_comment: Subject keywords (case-insensitive) that set the starting priority on new tickets, for tiers with a 'priorities' map.
_macros_comment: Canned replies (macros), visible to everyone when replying. 'set_status' is applied in the same click. Greetings avoid the contact's name: contacts without one get their email prefix as a name. Placeholders: {{ .Author.FirstName }}, {{ .Conversation.ReferenceNumber }}.

macros.name: Ask for bug details
macros.message:
Hi,

Thanks for reporting this. To help us reproduce it quickly, could you share:

  • Your workspace or project ID
  • The SDK and version (e.g. Web, React Native, Flutter, iOS, Android) and the platform or browser
  • The form name or ID
  • Steps to reproduce, and what you expected vs what happened
  • Screenshots or a screen recording, if possible

Once we have these we'll dig in right away.

Best,
{{ .Author.FirstName }}
Encatch Support
